io_driver_functions.notes: Raw DMA3 transfer primitive; busy-waits on DMA status; both callers target MMIO address 0x0D000000 (EEPROM data port).
Arms DMA-complete IRQ mask bit and queues a 3-word transfer descriptor before an EEPROM write.
Disarms the DMA-complete IRQ mask bit and clears the queued descriptor after an EEPROM write.
EEPROM block read: bounds-checks block index, serializes read-opcode+address bitstream via FUN_08023624, unpacks 64 returned serial bits into 4 big-endian u16 words (8 data bytes).
EEPROM block write: bounds-checks block index, serializes write-opcode+address+64 data bits in one FUN_08023624 transfer, arms/disarms DMA IRQ, polls EEPROM busy bit.
Read-back verification: reads the just-written block via FUN_080236a4 and compares word-by-word against the expected 8 bytes; not a checksum algorithm, a direct byte/word comparison.
Top-level write-with-retry entry point (up to 3 attempts of write+verify). No caller present anywhere in the traced 112-function callgraph; this is the save-flush API boundary of this packet's trace.

caller_chains.trigger_context: unknown (no caller of 0x08023888 present in ghidra/callgraph.json)
caller_chains.how_mapped: Traced bottom-up from the two MMIO-seed functions (0x080236a4, 0x08023754) flagged in ghidra/save_related_functions.c, following ghidra/callgraph.json caller/callee edges up to the single entry point 0x08023888, which has an empty callers list — the trace boundary. No game-specific RAM-buffer-building caller was found anywhere in the 112-function decompiled set; the other functions present (0x0801e3e8-0x0801fd40 family) were checked by MMIO-address grep and do not reference 0x0D000000, DMA3, or any FUN_08023xxx symbol, so they were excluded as save-path candidates.

open_questions: What in-RAM struct/address range does the save-record builder populate before calling FUN_08023888? Not present in this packet's trace (ghidra/callgraph.json shows 0x08023888 with no callers).
Is there a checksum/CRC at all? Three positional candidates (0x0C, 0x0E, 0x1BE) were tested against sum8/16 and xor8/16 over 5 ranges with no match; algorithm and covered range remain unknown.
Are EEPROM blocks 60-63 (0x1E0-0x1FF) ever written (second save slot, unlock flag, etc.), or permanently reserved/unused? Both available samples show them as 0xFF.
What is the byte-order and semantic meaning of the two tables at 0xA8-0xCF and 0xD0-0x19F?
Does the 1-byte field at offset 0x000 gate loading, or is it cosmetic?
Only one non-blank .sav sample is available in this packet; a second independent mutation is required before any checksum/field hypothesis can move from UNKNOWN/HYPOTHESIS to CONFIRMED.
